title: Front Doors
tagline: Four ways into the same models — and why reach and review burden rise together
hub_blurb: Compare four ways to use AI across seven faculty tasks, then choose the smallest tool that can finish each job.
card_blurb: The audience thinks “using AI” means a chat box. It is one surface out of four, and the least capable. A chat window, the agent already inside Docs or Word, a desktop coworker, a coding agent — set against 4 axes: what it can see, what it can do, whether it keeps going unwatched, and how much you must check. Then 7 real faculty jobs, and for each one the smallest door that finishes it and exactly what you hand over to get there.
description: **Front Doors** — a phone-first, single-file, offline teaching module about the *surfaces* through which a person can use AI, built for part three of the talk and running immediately after The Stranger: that one covered how to phrase the request, this one covers what to ask it with. Act I sets four doors — a chat window, an agent inside the tools you already have, a desktop coworker, a coding agent — against 4 axes, making 16 cells, each opening the reason, the vendor's own wording, an honesty label and a link to the page it came from. Act II converts “which is best” into “which fits this job”: 7 realistic faculty tasks against the same doors, 28 judgements in all, with the smallest sufficient door computed from the verdicts rather than typed, and every card ending in what you would have to hand over. Act III is the receipts — two product names that already moved in the six months before the check date, quoted from the vendors that moved them; a prediction of what will rot next and what will hold; the one row that is honestly uneven because Google has no consumer peer at door 3; and everything researched and left off. The argument the whole thing is built to carry is that going inward is not an upgrade: reach and review burden rise together, and the cheapest review in the table belongs to the humblest door, because it hands you a change to accept or reject instead of a finished thing to judge. Every product claim resolves to a first-party page and is labelled verified, reasoned or unconfirmed — 13 verified, 3 reasoned across the grid, 15 sources, 9 things cut — no prices anywhere on purpose, no vendor ranked, and a live self-test that proves all of it in front of the room.
